# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 17 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 17 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_017_page_001.jpg

---

1 Great are your judgments — too great to put into words. This is why undisciplined souls have always gone astray.

2 The lawless men believed they held the holy nation in their grip. But they were the ones in chains — fettered by darkness, imprisoned by endless night, locked under their own roofs, cut off from the eternal light of your providence.

3 They thought their secret sins could stay hidden. Instead, darkness scattered them, swallowed them in a black fog of forgetting, and left them shaking — haunted by visions they could not explain.

4 Even the rooms where they hid offered no protection from fear. Sounds crashed around them — sounds filled with dread. And out of the dark came phantoms: gloomy shapes with sullen, scowling faces.

5 No fire was strong enough to break through. Not even the brilliant blaze of the stars could pierce that horrible night.

6 Through it all there filtered only a single unnatural fire, spontaneous and terrifying. And in their fear the Egyptians decided that what they could see was worse than what they could not.

7 The clever tricks of their sorcerers were exposed as frauds. All their boasted wisdom collapsed into humiliation.

8 These were the people who promised to chase fear and sickness from troubled minds — now they themselves were gripped by a ridiculous, uncontrollable terror.

9 Even when nothing genuinely threatening was near them, they were unmanned by the slithering of reptiles and the hissing of snakes —

10 they died trembling, too afraid to so much as look at the air itself, though the air was all around them and could not be escaped.

11 That is the nature of wickedness: it is a coward. It condemns itself with its own inner voice. Pressed hard by conscience, it always imagines disaster worse than it is.

12 Fear is nothing more than this: a giving up of reason's defenses.

13 And when the inner resource runs dry, the mind exaggerates its ignorance of the cause — and that exaggeration becomes a worse torment than the cause itself.

14 So they lay through that powerless night — that night that rose from the depths of equally powerless Hades — trapped in the same helpless sleep,

15 driven now by monstrous, lurching apparitions, now paralyzed as their own souls gave way beneath them. Sudden and unexpected, terror seized them.

16 If any one of them stumbled and fell, he stayed where he fell — held down, imprisoned, as if by bars of iron, though no iron was there.

17 It made no difference who he was — a farmer, a shepherd, a laborer working out in the fields. Each was overtaken. Each endured a doom from which there was no escape. They were all shackled in the same chain of darkness.

18 Whether it was the whistling of the wind through branches, or birdsong floating melodiously through the spreading trees, or the rhythmic sound of rushing water —

19 or rocks shattering as they fell, or the unseen galloping of some leaping animal in the dark, or the full-throated roar of a wild beast, or the strange echo of a voice bouncing back from a hollow mountain — every sound shattered them with terror.

20 For the whole world outside was flooded with brilliant light, going about its business without interruption.

21 But over those people alone — only those people — a thick night had been stretched like a lid. It was a foretaste, an image of the darkness that was already waiting to receive them. Yet even so, they were a heavier burden to themselves than the darkness was.
